I understand why you like the rimless look—they’re designed with very little visible structure. But at around **-6.00D, none of the rimless frames in this catalog meets your prescription requirement**:

- Orbit&Co Line 482: compatible up to **-4.00D** [1]
- Orbit&Co Type 282: up to **-4.00D** [4]
- Basalt Form 448, Sundial Series 103, and Halcyon Type 404: up to **-3.50D** [2][3][5]

Rimless mounting means the lenses are drilled to attach directly to the temples and bridge. With a stronger minus prescription, lens shape and size matter: smaller lenses generally help reduce thickness, while larger or irregular shapes can increase it [A1]. The lens material also needs careful selection for drilled mounting; 1.74 high-index material is marked for high prescriptions because it can help with thinness, but it has lower tensile strength—resistance to pulling or breaking—than 1.60 and 1.67 materials in the cited table [A2][A3].

The **nearest catalog option** by shape and size is the **Halcyon Type 404**, a small, relatively regular round frame, but it is still rated only up to **-3.50D**, so it does **not** solve the prescription requirement [5][A1]. We don’t have a non-rimless frame listed here to offer as a true alternative. I’ve assumed your main distance power is approximately -6.00D; we should check the complete prescription and have the laboratory confirm whether a drilled rimless design is appropriate.
